evidence: src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts: constructor injects `@InjectRepository(CourseEntity) private readonly courseRepository: Repository<CourseEntity>` and enrol() calls `this.courseRepository.findOne(...)` and `this.courseRepository.save(entity)`, changing and saving course state outside the courses module.

src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts: `import { toCourse } from '../courses/courses.service'` borrows the courses entity-to-domain mapper, but the reverse step is written inline as `entity.enrolled = course.enrolled`, splitting the course mapping across modules.

src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts: enrol() maps with `this.enrolmentRepository.create({ ...enrolment })` while withdraw() maps with `new Enrolment(row.courseId, row.studentEmail, row.enrolledAt)`: two separate enrolment mappings and no shared mapper.

src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts: enrol() enforces `if (!studentEmail.includes('@')) throw new DomainError('invalid', ...)` and the duplicate check `enrolmentRepository.count(...) > 0` in the service, while the capacity rule goes through the domain via `course.admit()`, so rules are placed inconsistently.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The single file handles one concern (enrolment), but it uses its abstractions inconsistently and goes around the courses module. EnrolmentsService injects Repository<CourseEntity> and changes and saves course rows directly. It borrows the entity-to-domain helper toCourse from courses.service but writes the reverse mapping itself (entity.enrolled = course.enrolled), so the course mapping and persistence rule is split between two modules. Enrolment mapping is also done two ways: enrol spreads the domain object into enrolmentRepository.create({...enrolment}), while withdraw rebuilds it with new Enrolment(row.courseId, row.studentEmail, row.enrolledAt). There is no single mapper, unlike toCourse for courses. The email check (includes('@')) and the duplicate-enrolment rule are enforced in the service instead of in the Enrolment domain object, while the capacity rule correctly goes through course.admit(), so rule placement is inconsistent too. Confidence is moderate because the courses module and the Enrolment class are not visible.
